definitions.explanation: An orange fruit native to East Asia, eaten fresh when ripe or dried. Persimmons are a symbol of autumn in Japan.

examples.japanese: {庭|にわ}の{柿|かき}が{色|いろ}づいてきた。
examples.english: The persimmons in the garden are starting to ripen.

examples.japanese: {干|ほ}し{柿|がき}は{甘|あま}くて{美味|おい}しい。
examples.english: Dried persimmons are sweet and delicious.

examples.japanese: {渋柿|しぶがき}はそのまま{食|た}べられない。
examples.english: Astringent persimmons cannot be eaten as they are.

examples.japanese: {秋|あき}は{柿|かき}が{美味|おい}しい{季節|きせつ}だ。
examples.english: Autumn is the season when persimmons are delicious.

examples.japanese: {田舎|いなか}のおばあちゃんの{家|いえ}には{大|おお}きな{柿|かき}の{木|き}がある。
examples.english: There is a large persimmon tree at my grandmother's house in the countryside.

notes:
{柿|かき} refers to persimmons.

Types:
- {甘柿|あまがき} (sweet persimmon - can be eaten fresh)
- {渋柿|しぶがき} (astringent persimmon - must be dried or processed)
- {干|ほ}し{柿|がき} (dried persimmon)

Common expressions:
- {柿|かき}の{種|たね} (persimmon seed; also a type of rice cracker)
- {柿|かき}が{赤|あか}くなると{医者|いしゃ}が{青|あお}くなる (when persimmons turn red, doctors turn pale - persimmons are healthy)

Counter: {個|こ}

Cultural note:
Persimmon trees are common in Japanese gardens and countryside. The orange persimmons hanging from bare branches are an iconic autumn scene. {干|ほ}し{柿|がき} (dried persimmons) are made by peeling and hanging persimmons to dry, transforming astringent persimmons into a sweet treat. The famous haiku by Masaoka Shiki mentions persimmons: 「{柿|かき}{食|く}えば{鐘|かね}が{鳴|な}るなり{法隆寺|ほうりゅうじ}」
